explain.say: Sleep can look like switching off, but your brain stays busy all night. Scientists have found several important jobs that seem to need sleep.

faq.a: During sleep the brain replays the day's experiences and strengthens the connections for important ones, moving memories into long-term storage. Both deep sleep and REM sleep seem to play a part.
asks: Why do we remember better after sleep?

faq.q: Does the brain clean itself during sleep?
faq.a: Research in mice showed that during sleep, fluid flows through the brain much faster, washing away waste products made by busy brain cells. This cleaning system is called the glymphatic system.

faq.q: What does the body repair during sleep?
faq.a: In deep sleep the body releases growth hormone, which helps build and repair tissues such as muscles and bones. Breathing and heart rate slow, giving the body a rest.
asks: Does the body heal during sleep?
Why is deep sleep important for growth?

faq.q: What happens if you do not get enough sleep?
faq.a: After too little sleep, people find it harder to concentrate, remember things and control their mood, and their reaction times slow down.
asks: What does lack of sleep do?
Why do I feel bad without sleep?

faq.a: Almost all animals studied show some kind of sleep, from mammals and birds to fish and even fruit flies. Dolphins can rest one half of the brain at a time while the other half stays alert.

facts: The brain's waste-clearing glymphatic system was described in mice in 2012, and a 2013 study found it works much faster during sleep.
Dolphins can sleep with one half of the brain at a time.

quiz.say: Which of these is one job the brain does during sleep?
quiz.why: Sleep is when the brain replays and stores memories, among other maintenance jobs.

wrong.1: The brain stays active all night; in REM sleep it is nearly as busy as when awake.
wrong.2: The sleeping brain still uses a lot of energy.
